title: 3-round AES-128: Semi-square balance distinguisher

target.description: 3 inner AES rounds, without initial whitening and with MixColumns in every round, under fixed round keys. The parameter-independent round argument applies to the standard AES-128 schedule.

setting.key_relation: One unknown fixed key; the underlying inner-round property holds independently of schedule relations.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key restriction.
setting.plaintext_model: Fix every non-diagonal byte. Fix one chosen bit position in each of the four diagonal bytes and enumerate the other seven bits in each, giving 2^28 inputs.
setting.reference_model: Uniformly random permutation of the 128-bit block space, with the same classical chosen-plaintext access.

time.note: The paper proposes this distinguisher but gives no complete standalone evaluation budget.

data.note: One full structure for the stated property; repeated tests and a target advantage are not specified.

memory.note: No separate standalone distinguisher memory budget is stated.

preprocessing.note: No separately costed setup is stated.

success.description: Derived distinguishing-advantage lower bound for one fixed complete 2^28-input semi-square structure and the full 128-bit output-XOR test. Proposition6 makes AES acceptance one, under the stored three-inner-round convention. For one uniform random permutation on Q=2^128 blocks, condition on the first M-1 distinct outputs, M=2^28. At most one remaining block can make the complete XOR zero; its conditional probability is at most1/(Q-M+1). Taking the complement gives the displayed advantage bound. The input constants and common fixed bit position are selected before querying; no search over structures or coordinatewise independence is used. This is a new bound derived from the source construction, not an author-printed probability or balanced classification accuracy. Original unknown evaluation costs remain unknown.

components.description: AppendixA Proposition6: fixing the same bit position in four diagonal input bytes and enumerating the remaining28 bits gives zero XOR in every output byte after three complete AES rounds. This is a deterministic AES-side event, not an advantage against a random permutation.

review.scope: Verified exact source experiment, deterministic AES acceptance, ideal-permutation sampling without replacement and conservative whole-decision bound. Independently source-first and endpoint reviewed. This does not certify unknown resources, disputed source claims, attack reproduction or a new full-paper audit.

limitations: Results are transcribed from this source version. Full attack searches, costs and success probabilities have not been reproduced.
The source supplies no false-positive probability against random permutations for this exact structure.

Independent semi-square validation covers the algebraic balance, not random-permutation advantage, complete distinguisher cost or an attack reproduction. The two-fixed-bit failure is non-universal, not a claim that every smaller subset fails.
